scope: Read-only diagnosis following real catalog request failures; samples were collected sequentially, not atomically. No deployment, restart, heap change, heap dump, full GC, model request or additional catalog stress query was performed by this investigation.

jvmPerfdata.method: Read existing HotSpot /tmp/hsperfdata_*/1; no JVM attach, heap dump or forced GC
jvmPerfdata.boundary: Counters and used space are a later point-in-time sample; they do not locate the failed allocation or measure per-cache retained size. Collector counts are cumulative.

errors.stackBoundary: The observed OOM entries did not provide a usable allocation stack. An exact retained-object cause is not established.

catalog.countMethod: Existing gying-source PyMySQL runtime; SELECT COUNT(*) with status=ACTIVE AND deleted_at IS NULL; read-only transaction rolled back; 5-second statement limit

referenceProjection.boundary: Historical JSON field sizes are not current Java heap object sizes; absent projection fields were not counted.

host.boundary: Windows and Docker/Linux values are separately sampled and must not be added; available memory is not a future guarantee.

recoveryCandidate.boundary: Temporary recovery proposal only. User paused deployment. Requires a fresh memory/readiness check, preserved current image/configuration and rollback materials, normal graceful termination without force-kill, affected-service-only replacement, then serial real-entry verification. No capacity or stability conclusion has been measured.

notEstablished: Whether both lazy/eager text indexes were resident at failure
Whether cross-service cache rebuilds overlapped at failure
Whether the proposed memory increase alone is sufficient
Production quality improvement from the undeployed Agent candidate
